newsitem.title: UK: BBC extends "lifeline" to central Africa.
newsitem.headline: BBC extends "lifeline" to central Africa.

text.p: The British Broadcasting Corporation said on Friday its World Service radio was expanding local language broadcasts aimed at refugees displaced by the crisis in central Africa.
The programmes carry "humanitarian messages" such as pleas from people trying to find their families as well as news and current affairs from Zaire, Rwanda and neighbouring countries.

The BBC has broadcast a 15-minute programme each weekday in the Kinyarwanda and Kirundi languages since September 1994, a few months after the genocide of Tutsis and moderate Hutus in Rwanda, followed by an exodus of Hutus to Zaire.
From early December, the programmes, which begin at 1615 GMT and are broadcast on shortwave frequencies 11860 and 21490, will be extended to 30 minutes from 15 minutes.
The BBC said United Nations research showed that its programmes were seen as "the most trusted information source" by the refugees in central Africa.
